solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Brian joins mate, the one repairing Victorian book

indicators.note: repairing means putting something back together, so these letters are pieced into a new order

explanation.surface: A man called Brian teams up with a friend who is restoring an old nineteenth-century volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joins' is a link; 'repairing' rearranges BRIAN, MATE and THE ONE, all fifteen letters, into the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerome K. Jerome's comic novel of a Thames boating trip was published in 1889, in Queen Victoria's reign.

clue.text: Wonder if Maltese port flourishes around mid-December

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters are placed about the next piece
flourishes suggests waving about with a flourish, so the letters of the preceding words are shaken into a new order
mid- asks for the central letters of the word it is attached to

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a harbour in Malta thrives in the middle of December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wonder' is the definition, not a verb: 'flourishes' yields TPLEOFARTIS, and 'around' fits the December middle in after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: The temple at Ephesus was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

clue.text: Solitary person on part of crossword, taking minimum of effort to finish

parts.note: re means on, concerning, as in a business letter

indicators.note: taking, with to finish, says a letter is carried off and put down at the end
to finish names the end of the word as where the carried letter goes

parts.note: the clues are a part of any crossword

indicators.note: minimum of asks for the smallest part, the opening letter, of the next word

explanation.surface: A loner tackles a crossword clue but puts in hardly any work to complete it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... to finish' carries the effort letter from its place in the clue-word to the end; 'part of crossword' is plural in sense, as clues are what a crossword is made of.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse is someone who lives alone and shuns company, a hermit.

clue.text: Cosmetic reconstructing — see why hosts bother

indicators.note: hosts says the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside them
reconstructing means building afresh, so the letters of the next two words are reassembled

parts.note: ado means fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A make-up product being remade, prompting the question of why its makers trouble themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconstructing' gives EYESHW; 'hosts' looks like people entertaining but means holding the bother word inside, just before the final W.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye shadow is a coloured make-up applied to the eyelids.

clue.text: Preferred section of the lecture

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Choosing the part of a talk one likes best.
explanation.definitionFit: Elect as an adjective means chosen or picked out, as in the president-elect.

clue.text: Please remain with ailing fogy in case of financial promise

indicators.note: in case of says the promise surrounds the other letters like a case

parts.note: an IOU is a written promise to pay a debt
to be is to remain or exist

indicators.note: ailing means unwell, out of sorts, so the letters of the next word are disordered

explanation.surface: An unwell old fogy being asked to stay put while a debt pledge is in force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ailing' gives GOFY; 'in case of' reads as a legal phrase but means the promise forms a case around the rest. 'Please' is a plea here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a heartfelt plea, used just as please is when begging someone.

clue.text: Blue trailer, regularly sublet

parts.note: a trailer is an advertisement for a film, an ad

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A sad caravan being let out to another tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth and sixth letters of SUBLET, U L T. 'Trailer' looks like a vehicle but is a film advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue films and adult films are both euphemisms for pornographic material.

clue.text: Dated in France, where pair joined navy

parts.note: ou is the French word for where
a pair is two
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Recalling a time in France when a couple signed up for the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Outworn means worn out by long use, hence old-fashioned or obsolete.

clue.text: Sporting contest for actress Doris and two siblings?

definitions.text: Sporting contest for actress Doris and two siblings?

parts.words: Sporting contest for actress Doris and two siblings?
parts.note: the actress Doris Day plus two brothers or sisters would make three people surnamed Day, competing in a horse-riding contest that lasts three days

explanation.surface: Imagining a sports event for the actress Doris Day and her brother and sister.
explanation.walkthrough: Doris Day was an American actress; the riddle punningly counts three Days. Eventing is the equestrian sport of dressage, cross-country and show jumping, often held over three days.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in eventing, the horse trials held over three days, is called by this name.

clue.text: Spice keeps breaking the knife

indicators.note: keeps says the spice holds the other letters within it

parts.note: mace is a spice made from the husk of nutmeg

indicators.note: breaking means smashing, so the letters of the next word are broken up

explanation.surface: A seasoning that stops something shattering the blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' gives HET; 'keeps' makes the spice hold it. 'Spice' could suggest a Spice Girl, but it is the seasoning.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy blade used for cutting vegetation.

clue.text: Circle line avoids same peak

indicators.note: avoids says the line keeps out of the word, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: equal means the same
a tor is a rocky hilltop or peak

explanation.surface: A London Underground route that steers clear of the same summit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle line is a London Underground route, which hides that 'Circle' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The equator is the great circle of latitude around the Earth's middle.

clue.text: Body of water Berkshire community initially ignored

indicators.note: initially ignored says the opening letter of the town is left off

parts.note: Slough is a town in the English county of Berkshire

explanation.surface: A lake overlooked at first by a town in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A lough is an Irish lake or sea inlet, the Irish counterpart of the Scottish loch.

clue.text: Set to work fixing such an engine?

indicators.note: fixing means mending, so the letters of the preceding words are put right in a new order

explanation.surface: Getting down to repairing a motor of a particular type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixing' rearranges SET TO WORK, and the whole clue also describes the engine being mended.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-stroke is a type of internal combustion engine completing its cycle in two piston movements.

clue.text: Initially observe main beast of burden not bearing right

indicators.note: Initially asks for the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: key means main or principal, as in a key point

indicators.note: not says the bearing is removed from the animal

parts.note: a donkey is a working animal that carries loads
N, north, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Watching the chief pack animal, which is not carrying anything on its right side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' looks like part of the bearing but is the definition, said as an interjection: DONKEY without N gives DOKEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal exclamations of agreement, like all right or OK.

clue.text: Australian resident taking punch before a party, one hears

indicators.note: before puts the punch ahead of what follows

parts.note: KO, a knockout, is a decisive punch
Lab is short for the Labour Party
the ear is the organ one hears with

explanation.surface: An Australian downing a drink before a celebration, as a listener tells it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one hears' looks like a sound-alike signal but is simply EAR; 'punch' is a blow, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The koala is a tree-dwelling marsupial native to Australia.

clue.text: One marches in army for patron at Christmas

indicators.note: in says the marcher goes inside the army

parts.note: SA is the Salvation Army
ants march in columns, army ants especially

explanation.surface: A soldier on parade in the forces, standing in for a festive benefactor.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Claus is the bearer of gifts at Christmas, a patron saint figure from St Nicholas.

clue.text: Monster abused cash to obtain dodgy building

indicators.note: to obtain says the rearranged letters take the building inside them
abused means misused, so the letters of the next word are mishandled

parts.note: a squat is a building occupied illegally

explanation.surface: A villain misused money to buy a shady property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abused' gives SACH, and 'to obtain' has those letters take the dodgy building inside, after the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The sasquatch, or Bigfoot, is a legendary ape-like creature of North American forests.

clue.text: US politician once again defends government

indicators.note: defends says the word for again guards the letter inside it

parts.note: anew means again, afresh

explanation.surface: An American politician once more stands up for the administration.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiro Agnew was US vice-president under Nixon, resigning in 1973.

clue.text: Woman turned colour when laughing

indicators.note: turned says the colour word is flipped round

parts.note: tan is a yellowish-brown colour
as means when
ha is the sound of laughter

explanation.surface: A woman went pale or red when she burst out laughing.
explanation.definitionFit: Natasha is a woman's first name, a Russian pet form of Natalia.

clue.text: Cups are put inside cooker by this person — something a fool would do?

indicators.note: put inside says the cups go within the cooker

parts.note: an Aga is a brand of heavy range cooker found in British country kitchens
mugs are drinking cups
me is the setter speaking of themself

explanation.surface: Someone leaving cups in the oven: a silly thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a big British range cooker; 'put inside' opens it for the cups, and 'by this person' adds the setter after.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug's game is an idiom for a pointless or foolish activity, a mug being a dupe.

clue.text: Social worker, one month, turned up WI member?

parts.note: the ant is a social insect and a worker
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue says the month is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Aug is short for August

explanation.surface: A social worker joins a women's group one month.
explanation.walkthrough: WI suggests the Women's Institute, a British community club for women; here it is the West Indies.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is a Caribbean island in the West Indies.

clue.text: Bird, female, obtains watering-hole somewhere in farm

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: obtains says the hen takes the next piece inside

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
a bar is a drinking place, a watering-hole

explanation.surface: A female bird gets a drink somewhere on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird, female' looks like one bird but gives two pieces, TIT and HEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe barn was a farm building storing the tenth of produce owed to the church.

clue.text: From the books of unknown person — disturbing, upsetting humour

indicators.note: disturbing says the unknown breaks into the turned word
upsetting in a down clue says the word is turned upside down

parts.note: bile was one of the four bodily humours
X stands for an unnamed or unknown person, as in Mr X

explanation.surface: Lines from someone's library: a mystery author with unsettling, upsetting jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns BILE into ELIB, and 'disturbing' puts X into it after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Ex lib., short for ex libris, is the Latin bookplate phrase meaning from the library of.

clue.text: Island chiefs in natural attire unadvisedly run uphill

indicators.note: chiefs in asks for the head letters of each following word

explanation.surface: Tribal leaders in their natural dress unwisely jog up a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru is a small Pacific island nation in Micronesia.

clue.text: Canadian police loosened doctor free

indicators.note: loosened says the doctor is set free from the word, so those letters drop out

parts.note: a Mountie is a Royal Canadian Mounted Police officer
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A Canadian Mountie released a doctor without charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie is to free something from its bonds.

clue.text: Flash trader squanders last wine

parts.note: a mo, a moment, is a flash

indicators.note: squanders last says the final letter of the trader is lost

parts.note: a seller is a trader

explanation.surface: A showy dealer wastes the last of the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Moselle is a white wine from the Mosel valley in Germany.

clue.text: University training's before 0800, when lacking energy, irritated

indicators.note: before places the training ahead of the time

parts.note: PT is physical training

indicators.note: lacking says the energy letter is missing from the time

parts.note: 0800 is eight o'clock in the morning
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Early-morning university exercise leaves a tired student cross.
explanation.walkthrough: PT, physical training, is gym class; 0800 is eight o'clock, giving EIGHT, less E.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptight is informal for tense, anxious or irritated.

clue.text: Mark heads for busking outlet — difficult market for 1960s pop

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin

indicators.note: heads for asks for the opening letters of the next two words

parts.note: rough means hard or difficult
a fair is a market

explanation.surface: A street musician sets off for a tough market pitch to play 1960s songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon and Garfunkel's version of the old ballad was a hit in the 1960s.
